Sibuna 1.0.0-beta.1 is the first beta of Sibuna 1.0, a web firewall and anti-crawler
daemon written in Rust. It sits in front of an origin as a reverse proxy, or beside an
ingress as a forward-auth engine, and admits browsers that prove work while it denies
known automation, injected payloads, floods and honeypot hits before they reach the origin.

Highlights:
- Proof-of-work admission: Cohen-Pietrzak proof of sequential work (default) or bit-level
  Hashcash, solved in the browser by an embedded WebAssembly solver and verified natively.
- Stateless challenges and keyed-BLAKE3 session tokens bound to the client (Ed25519
  optional); only solved challenges occupy memory.
- Two surfaces in one binary: Gate (challenge, policy, limits) and Shield (adds semantic
  SQL injection, XSS, path traversal and command injection inspection).
- Declarative JSON policy, bot signatures, CIDR reputation, GCRA rate limits per client
  and per rule, honeypot bans; request parsing and classification do not allocate on the
  warm path.
- Optional storage: SQLite for one node (--data-dir) with policies, reputation, forensics
  with full-text search and campaign similarity.
- Optional console (--console): dashboards with a country globe, incident investigation,
  policy editing, users with TOTP, scoped API tokens, audit browsing, GeoIP imports and
  the `sibuna console` command line client.

Downloads (all for this tag, verify them with SHA256SUMS):
- Linux x86-64 and ARM64: static musl archives, Debian .deb and RPM .rpm packages.
- Arch Linux x86-64: sibuna-bin .pkg.tar.zst, installed with pacman -U.
- macOS Apple Silicon and Intel: unsigned archives, macOS 12 or later.
- Windows x86-64: sibuna.exe in a ZIP archive, Windows 10 or Server 2016 or later.
- FreeBSD 15.1 amd64: .pkg, installed with pkg add.
- OpenBSD 7.9 amd64: .tgz, installed with pkg_add -D unsigned.
- Homebrew formula sibuna.rb for macOS and Linux, installing the archives above.
- Helm chart helm-sibuna-1.0.0-beta.1.tgz and the image ghcr.io/insanai/sibuna:1.0.0-beta.1
  for amd64 and arm64 (digest in IMAGE-DIGEST.txt).
- The source bundle sibuna-1.0.0-beta.1-source.tar.gz.

Every archive and package carries LICENSE, NOTICE, LICENSES/ (with the third-party crate
list THIRD-PARTY-RUST.txt), README.md, SECURITY.md and sibuna.build.json, which records
the commit, Rust target, compiler and the SHA-256 of the executable. Each executable was
started and checked on its own platform before publication, and the packages were
installed, reinstalled and removed on Debian, Fedora, Arch, FreeBSD and OpenBSD.

Linux packages install the account `sibuna` and a stopped systemd unit. Set the origin
(an IP literal) in /etc/sibuna/service.env, then start the service; it listens on
127.0.0.1:8080 and creates a private admission seed in /var/lib/sibuna on first start.
Configuration, seed and state survive upgrade and removal. BSD packages install only the
command and its documents; they create no service, account or state.

Known limitations of this beta:
- The release executables have SQLite storage and the console, but no PostgreSQL
  support. Clusters on a shared PostgreSQL database need a build from source with
  `cargo build --release -p sibuna --features postgres-tls`.
- The assets are not signed. macOS archives are not notarized: remove the quarantine
  attribute of a browser download with `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine sibuna`. The
  Windows executable is not Authenticode-signed and has no Windows service integration.
- Windows has no file mode bits, so Sibuna does not check that key and credential files
  are private there; restrict them with ACLs. The console's process memory and CPU
  gauges are available on Linux only.
- Sibuna does not terminate TLS; put it behind an ingress that does. Its ingress recipes
  for forward-auth (Caddy, Nginx) are not yet tested against live ingresses.
- The console's isolation under load with eight active dashboards has not been measured
  yet, and its WebAssembly module (about 700 KiB) is above the 640 KiB review threshold.
- This is a pre-release: options, storage schema and console APIs may still change
  before 1.0.0. Back up the data directory before upgrading.

Sibuna is free software under LGPL-3.0-or-later. Report vulnerabilities privately through
https://github.com/insanai/sibuna/security/advisories/new (see SECURITY.md).

Documentation: https://insanai.github.io/sibuna/
Source: https://github.com/insanai/sibuna/tree/v1.0.0-beta.1
